issues_detected.description: The description states that this Beta release includes 'Perturb-seq data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment', but no MDA-MB-468 Perturb-seq file collection is listed among the ten archives (only cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip and cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_raw_sra.zip are present). external_resources and confidential_elements record the MDA-MB-468 Perturb-seq deposition as embargoed, which contradicts its inclusion in the release contents.
issues_detected.recommendation: Reconcile the description's release-contents statement with file_collections: either state that MDA-MB-468 Perturb-seq is embargoed and not distributed in this release, or add the corresponding file collection.

issues_detected.description: The documented preprocessing pipeline (node2vec PPI embedding, HPA image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, community detection, GSAI annotation) produces cell maps, which known_limitations, anomalies and discouraged_uses all state are NOT included in this release. How the distributed processed_data packages (AP-MS, SEC-MS, Perturb-seq atlas) were themselves derived from raw acquisitions is not described.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add preprocessing_strategies entries covering the derivation of the released processed_data packages (spectral search and quantification for AP-MS/SEC-MS, read alignment and cell calling for Perturb-seq), distinguishing them from the downstream cell-map pipeline.

issues_detected.description: No software is named that produced or transformed the released data. The named tooling falls entirely into excluded roles: node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF, GPT-4/GSAI and the Cell Mapping Toolkit belong to a pipeline the record states produced cell maps not in this release; FAIRSCAPE produced the RO-Crate packaging and provenance metadata; the 10x Genomics kit, confocal microscope and pipetting robot are capture instrumentation; UVA Dataverse is the hosting platform.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the mass-spectrometry search/quantification software and the single-cell processing software (with versions) that produced the distributed AP-MS, SEC-MS and Perturb-seq atlas packages, attaching them via used_software on the relevant processing strategies.

issues_detected.description: Content-level file formats inside the distributed ZIP archives are not specified. distribution_formats declares only the container (ZIP, application/zip) and the metadata package (RO-Crate, application/ld+json); raw_data_sources gives 'Multi-channel confocal microscopy image files' without naming a standard (e.g. OME-TIFF, mzML, MTX/H5AD). No character encoding is stated.
issues_detected.recommendation: Declare per-collection content formats and media types (image, mass-spectrometry and single-cell matrix formats) and character encoding for text-based files, in addition to the ZIP container.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata is provided: the variables slot is absent entirely, and no data dictionary describes the columns of the distributed tabular components (AP-MS/SEC-MS result tables, Perturb-seq atlas). is_tabular: false is asserted at dataset level, but processed_data packages plainly contain tabular content.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variables entries with identifiers and descriptions for the columns of the processed AP-MS, SEC-MS and Perturb-seq atlas tables.

issues_detected.description: No errata and no change description for this release. errata is absent; updates.update_details states only future cadence ('quarterly ... through the end of the project in November 2026') and carries no release or derivation information. The only change narrative in the record concerns an earlier release (related_datasets note on the June 2025 revision), not what June 2026 added over October 2025.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add errata and/or a release-note entry in updates.update_details describing what changed in the June 2026 release relative to the October 2025 release.

issues_detected.description: Version ordering is confusing: this June 2026 release is version 2.0, while version_access records the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases as version 2.1. A newer release carries a lower version string than its predecessors.
issues_detected.recommendation: Clarify that each quarterly release is a separate Dataverse dataset with an independent internal version counter, or align version strings across the series.

issues_detected.description: Stated update frequency 'quarterly' is not borne out by the release dates recorded: March 2025, June 2025, October 2025, then June 2026 — an eight-month interval between the last two.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the actual cadence observed, or note the reason for the interval between the October 2025 and June 2026 releases.

issues_detected.description: Deidentification is asserted by rationale rather than by a named method: is_deidentified.deidentification_details argues the data 'cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject' because they are non-clinical tissue culture. No standard (Safe Harbor, expert determination) is invoked, while subpopulations.notes does disclose donor attributes for both lines (MDA-MB-468: 51-year-old black female, metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma; KOLF2.1J: healthy male Northern European donor).
issues_detected.recommendation: State the basis of the deidentification determination explicitly (cell-line provenance and absence of linkable donor identifiers) and note that the disclosed donor attributes are those published with the public Cellosaurus/HipSci cell-line records.

issues_detected.description: The dedicated download_url slot is empty. Access is reachable only via the page landing URL plus platform access instructions carried in distribution_formats.notes (per-file direct download under a 1.9 GB limit; Dataverse Data Access API for programmatic access).
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the Dataverse Data Access API endpoint for the persistent identifier.

issues_detected.description: No release-level instance counts for the imaging modality. Project-level figures (53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 proteins) are explicitly withheld in source_caveats as project-wide, and the per-condition protein count (464/563) is attributed to prior releases rather than to this one.
issues_detected.recommendation: Report the number of images and proteins of interest actually contained in the three June 2026 immunofluorescence archives.

issues_detected.description: acquisition_methods states AP-MS was acquired 'under three conditions (untreated, paclitaxel treated, vorinostat treated)', while the release distributes AP-MS only for the two treated conditions. The acquisition text describes project-level acquisition rather than release contents, which is defensible but not signposted.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mark acquisition_methods entries that describe project-wide acquisition as distinct from what the release distributes.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C is well formed and the 10.18130 prefix is the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) registrant, consistent with publisher ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia) and with the page URL host dataverse.lib.virginia.edu — identifier, publisher and landing page agree.

All three NIH award numbers parse cleanly against NIH conventions: 1OT2OD032742-01 (new award, OT2 activity code, OD institute), 3OT2OD032742-01S2 (revision/supplement S2 of the same core project) and 5U54HG012513-02 (non-competing continuation, U54, NHGRI), the last correctly attributed to the Bridge2AI Bridge Center rather than to CM4AI itself.

The Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia is recorded as a grantor with an acknowledgement note and no grants block, which is the correct representation for non-grant institutional support and is not a missing-award defect.

Licensing is internally coherent across three slots: license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission no_commercial_use, and ip_restrictions naming the copyright holders (Regents of the University of California; Stanford for raw image data) and the separate commercial negotiation path — the restrictiveness matches in all three.

Human-subjects logic is coherent throughout: involves_human_subjects false, at_risk_groups_included false, sensitive_elements_present false, no informed_consent or participant_privacy slots, and direct_collection.is_direct false with the explanation that all material derives from established cell lines (RRID:CVCL_0419, RRID:CVCL_B5P3). Nothing in the record asserts human participation that governance fields then fail to support.
Cell-line RRIDs are correctly formed Cellosaurus identifiers (RRID:CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468, RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J), giving unambiguous provenance for both biological substrates.

Bias, sampling and impact documentation are mutually reinforcing rather than duplicative: sampling_strategies asserts is_representative false with a why_not_representative rationale, known_biases records selection_bias and sampling_bias with affected_subsets, and future_use_impacts carries the downstream generalizability consequence — the same limitation is traced through three layers.
total_file_count: 10 matches the ten file_collections exactly, and every collection carries an MD5 checksum, an issue date and a collection_type distinguishing raw_data, processed_data and metadata.

Temporal ordering is consistent: created_on 2025-02-27 precedes issued 2026-06-17, which precedes last_updated_on 2026-07-15, and the latter matches the stated publication date of the three immunofluorescence archives.

The record is unusually disciplined about source conflict: source_caveats and per-field source_caveats declare where sources disagree (Sali's affiliation, protein counts across releases, project-level vs release-level figures, rounded file sizes) and decline to assert values rather than inventing them.

Governance is concretely staffed rather than abstractly asserted: data_governance names a Data Access Committee with a named contact and an access_review_process, regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact names the same person, and both ethical review contacts appear as creators with matching notes.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; prior releases cited by DOI (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM)
sub_elements.quality_note: A single persistent identifier is used consistently as id, doi and latest_version_doi, and resolves to the landing page given in page. Sibling releases are each identified by their own DOI, so a user can pin an exact release.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Format matches 10.XXXX/...; prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) registrant, plausible and consistent with publisher ROR:0153tk833 and the dataverse.lib.virginia.edu landing page. Cell-line RRIDs (RRID:CVCL_0419, RRID:CVCL_B5P3) are well-formed Cellosaurus identifiers, though they identify substrates rather than the dataset.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description of ~1,400 characters naming the four modalities, both cell lines, the treatment arms, the release contents, the RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE packaging and the nine-institution collaboration
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: it enumerates what this release contains modality by modality rather than describing the project in the abstract, and states the programme context (Bridge2AI Functional Genomics Grand Challenge).
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Content is semantically appropriate to a multimodal molecular cell-biology dataset; technical terms (Perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS, immunofluorescence, iPSC differentiation) are used correctly. One mismatch against file_collections is flagged as a consistency issue (MDA-MB-468 Perturb-seq claimed but not distributed).

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 29 terms including AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, single-cell RNA sequencing, protein-protein interaction, protein localization, MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, iPSC, breast cancer, paclitaxel, vorinostat, CRISPR/Cas9, Bridge2AI, CM4AI, subcellular imaging
sub_elements.quality_note: Well above the five-keyword threshold and spread across the axes a searcher would use: assay/method, cell line, perturbagen, biological entity, disease area and programme. Both spelled-out and abbreviated forms are given (e.g. 'size exclusion chromatography' and 'SEC-MS'), which helps recall.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Every keyword is corroborated elsewhere in the record; none is a generic filler term. Programme context (Bridge2AI, CM4AI) is inferable from quoted keyword values, as required.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections: ten entries each with id, name, path, collection_type, compression, issued date, description and MD5
sub_elements.quality_note: The landing page is a well-formed Dataverse persistent-identifier URL, and the resource structure below it is fully enumerated: each of the ten archives has a stable fragment identifier, a filename, a role (raw_data / processed_data / metadata) and a checksum, so a user can verify what they retrieved.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URL structure and host are plausible and match the DOI prefix registrant. Fragment identifiers (doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#ifimages-untreated etc.) are consistently constructed from the dataset DOI.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: five entries with relationship_type is_new_version_of (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX), is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311) and is_referenced_by (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734), each with an explanatory note
sub_elements.quality_note: The release is explicitly positioned in its quarterly series and against its describing preprint, with typed relationships rather than bare links. parent_datasets is absent, but the versioning lineage that matters here is fully expressed through typed relationships to the predecessor releases.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are used semantically correctly: the three predecessor releases are is_new_version_of, the describing preprint is_described_by, the companion atlas paper is_referenced_by. All target DOIs are well formed (10.18130 Dataverse, 10.1101 bioRxiv).

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spells out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 clause by clause (Attribution, NonCommercial, ShareAlike, no additional restrictions) with a citation obligation; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; ip_restrictions.restrictions names the Regents of the University of California as copyright holder, Stanford for raw spatial proteomics images, the commercial negotiation route, and MTA availability of the KOLF2.1J line
sub_elements.quality_note: A reuser can determine both what they may do and whom to approach for anything outside it, including the non-obvious detail that copyright is split by data package. The software licences (BSD-3 for the Tools pipeline, MIT for FAIRSCAPE) are correctly separated from the data licence.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: License name, enumerated clauses and the controlled data_use_permission value agree; ip_restrictions is consistent with, and adds specificity to, the NonCommercial clause. No over- or under-restrictive mismatch detected.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records the dataset as not FDA regulated, not involving human subjects, and comprising de-identified samples'; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact: Jillian Parker; data_governance.committee_contact: Jillian Parker with committee_name 'Data Access Committee' and an access_review_process; confidential_elements records the pre-publication embargo on Perturb-seq depositions
sub_elements.quality_note: The regulatory determination is stated affirmatively on three axes (FDA, human subjects, deidentification) rather than left blank, a named governance contact is given in both the regulatory and governance slots, and the one genuine access constraint — the embargo on specific depositions — is identified by modality and cell line.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: No confidentiality_level enum, hipaa_compliant or other_compliance value is supplied; HIPAA is not germane to non-clinical cell-line data, so its absence is appropriate, but a formal confidentiality classification would still be expected. Governance contact agrees across regulatory_restrictions and data_governance, and matches creator ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: page: Dataverse persistent-identifier URL; distribution_formats.notes: 'Individual files below the repository's 1.9 GB download limit may be downloaded directly; the dataset as a whole is too large to download as a single ZIP, and the Dataverse Data Access API is offered for programmatic access'; per-file path and MD5 for all ten archives
sub_elements.quality_note: Scored on the 'platform access instructions' branch of the criterion. The instructions are specific and operationally useful — they name the access route, state the per-file size ceiling, warn that whole-dataset ZIP download will fail, and give filenames and checksums to verify against.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The dedicated download_url slot is empty and no API endpoint URI is given, recorded as a low-severity completeness issue. Access is nonetheless determinate: the landing page resolves from the DOI and the retrieval mechanism is named.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format 'ZIP archive' / media_type application/zip, and format 'RO-Crate metadata package' / media_type application/ld+json; dataset-level compression: zip; each file_collection carries compression: zip; release metadata archive carries conforms_to: RO-Crate and conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]
sub_elements.quality_note: Two distribution formats are declared with correct MIME types, and the packaging standard is identified by both a free-text and an enumerated value. The record is explicit that RO-Crate provenance packaging travels with the data.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: application/zip and application/ld+json are correct media types for the stated formats. Content-level formats inside the archives (image, mass-spectrometry, single-cell matrix) are not declared — flagged as a medium-severity completeness issue rather than scored here, since this sub-element asks for distribution formats and file types, which are supplied.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: five typed entries; external_resources: eleven entries covering four MassIVE depositions (SEC-MS iPSC, SEC-MS MDA-MB-468, AP-MS paclitaxel, AP-MS vorinostat), the NCBI BioProject/SRA deposition with its embargo restriction, Figshare, https://cm4ai.org, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with readthedocs documentation, https://fairscape.github.io, https://integrativemodeling.org, https://ndexbio.org
sub_elements.quality_note: Exceptionally thorough: the underlying primary depositions are enumerated per modality with archival: true flags, embargo status is attached to the affected resource rather than stated generically, and tooling, portal and network-sharing endpoints are all reachable.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All URLs are well-structured and their domains are plausible for the named resources. MassIVE and SRA are the domain-appropriate repositories for mass-spectrometry and sequence data respectively, so the routing of each modality is semantically correct.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated (ZIP, RO-Crate), page resolves to a public Dataverse landing page with ten named archives, and the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence explicitly permits share and adapt.
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Users are free to share ... and adapt (remix, transform, and build upon the material)' subject to Attribution, NonCommercial and ShareAlike
sub_elements.quality_note: Reuse is affirmatively permitted and the permissions are enumerated rather than named by reference alone, so a reuser can determine compliance without consulting the licence deed. The NonCommercial limit and its negotiation route are clearly stated.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Licence identifier, enumerated permissions and data_use_permission enum are mutually consistent; ShareAlike obligation is correctly propagated to derivatives.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see sub-element 1).
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: 'ZIP archive' (application/zip) and 'RO-Crate metadata package' (application/ld+json); file_collections[release-metadata].conforms_to: RO-Crate with conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; description: 'packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework'
sub_elements.quality_note: RO-Crate with a JSON-LD media type is a genuine community packaging standard rather than a nominal format declaration, and it is asserted with a controlled enumeration value. Scored 1 on that basis.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Weakened by two gaps recorded as issues: the content formats inside the ZIPs are unnamed (raw_data_sources says only 'Multi-channel confocal microscopy image files'), and no character encoding is stated. A reuser can open the packages but cannot predict the internal file types before download.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see sub-element 1).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; file_collections[release-metadata]: conforms_to: RO-Crate, conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; instances use ontology CURIEs B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/58/59/64 and B2AI_TOPIC:15/26/34
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is asserted at three levels — the datasheet's own schema, the data package's RO-Crate standard, and Bridge2AI substrate/topic ontology terms on every instance — with the record honestly confining the RO-Crate claim to the metadata archive rather than over-claiming it for the image and mass-spectrometry content.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The w3id URI and the RO_CRATE enum are well formed; CURIE prefixes are used consistently. source_caveats explicitly explains why no dataset-level conforms_to is asserted, which is a correct rather than evasive scoping decision.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see sub-element 1), so this sub-element is scored rather than excluded.
sub_elements.evidence: No variables slot anywhere in the record; is_tabular: false; no data dictionary in file_collections, whose descriptions characterise each archive's biological content but not its columns or fields
sub_elements.quality_note: Nothing describes the variable-level structure of the distributed processed data. The AP-MS, SEC-MS and Perturb-seq atlas packages are inherently tabular result sets, so a reuser cannot determine column identifiers, units or semantics without opening the archives.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: is_tabular: false is coherent with the absence of variables at dataset level, but it is inconsistent with the processed_data packages' evident tabular content — recorded as a completeness issue. Scored 0 on absence of the evidence this sub-element requires.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: five categories with examples (AI-ready research data, model training, cellular process analysis, perturbation/disease analysis, interpretable ML with a usage_notes on downstream human-genomics applications); prohibited_uses: 'not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval'; discouraged_uses: integrated cell-map analysis (maps not in this release) and use without domain expertise
sub_elements.quality_note: All three registers are populated and each is substantive. The discouraged_uses entries are especially useful because they steer users away from precisely the misreading this interim release invites — expecting computed cell maps — rather than offering generic caution.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Guidance is consistent with the data type and with known_limitations; the clinical prohibition is proportionate for non-clinical cell-line research data and does not contradict the open CC BY-NC-SA licence.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition FAILS on external evidence: E1 description and keywords name cell lines (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J iPSC) and never participants, patients or clinical research; E8 collection_mechanisms describe mass spectrometers, confocal microscopy, a 10x Genomics kit and a pipetting robot, with no recruitment. Governance condition is MET on E2 evidence: regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact names Jillian Parker, and data_governance (also an E2 sub-element 2 field) documents a Data Access Committee with an access_review_process constraining distribution and requiring separate licence negotiation for commercial use. That is a governance constraint that applies, distinct from the block's negative regulatory statements, which on their own would not be a constraint. Applicability rests on E1/E8/E2 fields, not on Element 4's own fields.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries with review_details and contact_person (Vardit Ravitsky; Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon, described as working with the project's Ethics module on guidelines, best practices and governance milestones); human_subject_research.ethics_review_board gives both reviewers' contact e-mail addresses; human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance records the formal determination; data_governance.committee_contact: Jillian Parker
sub_elements.quality_note: For a dataset with no human participants, the oversight actually available is a named ethics function and a governance committee, and both are documented with named, contactable individuals and a description of the Ethics module's remit. A reader can identify who reviewed the release and whom to raise an ethical concern with — the actionable core of this sub-element.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: No IRB number is present, which is correct rather than missing: involves_human_subjects is false and the record states the determination explicitly, so no IRB approval is expected. data_protection_impacts is absent; a DPIA is not expected where no personal data is processed. Ethics contacts are corroborated by matching creator entries (ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153).

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same determination as sub-element 1: human-subjects condition fails on E1/E8 evidence, governance condition is met on E2 evidence (regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact plus data_governance's Data Access Committee and access_review_process). Deidentification can apply to donor-derived material, so the governance disjunct opens this sub-element.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'CM4AI data are non-clinical, deriving from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject. The June 2026 release record states that samples are de-identified and that the dataset does not involve human subjects.'
sub_elements.quality_note: The record states both the determination and the reasoning that supports it — non-clinical tissue-culture origin, no feasible linkage to an individual with current knowledge — which is the substantive answer for donor-derived cell-line material. It is not boilerplate and it tells a reuser what identifiability risk they are inheriting.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: No named standard (Safe Harbor, expert determination, k-anonymity) is invoked, and subpopulations.notes does publish donor attributes for both lines; these are the publicly catalogued Cellosaurus/HipSci descriptors rather than newly disclosed identifiers, but the tension is recorded as a low-severity content_accuracy issue. Deidentification claim is consistent with sensitive_elements_present: false and with involves_human_subjects: false.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition fails on external evidence: E1 description and keywords describe established human cell lines and their differentiated derivatives, naming no participants, patients or clinical research; E8 collection_mechanisms describe instrumentation only, with no participant recruitment (corroborated by direct_collection.is_direct: false, 'Data were not collected from individuals'). The governance disjunct does not reach this sub-element: a Data Access Committee over a dataset with no participants does not create participants whose privacy could be protected. Determination rests on E1/E8 fields, not on the absent participant_privacy slot.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk are absent; there are no participants in this dataset whose privacy could be protected or whose re-identification risk could be assessed
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Scoring 0 here would measure the dataset's subject matter — cell lines rather than people — instead of its documentation quality.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Exclusion is grounded in positive external evidence of non-participation, not in the emptiness of this sub-element's own fields, so the anti-circular rule is not engaged.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition fails on the same external evidence: E1 names cell lines only; E8 collection_mechanisms describe mass spectrometry, confocal microscopy, a 10x Genomics single-cell kit and a pipetting robot, with no recruitment of participants. The governance disjunct does not reach this sub-element. Determination rests on E1/E8 fields, not on the absent informed_consent slot.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent is absent; no individuals were enrolled, so no consent procedure, consent type or withdrawal mechanism exists to document
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. The record's own ip_restrictions note that the KOLF2.1J line is distributed to not-for-profit organisations under a simple MTA, i.e. material governance rather than participant consent, which is the appropriate instrument for this material.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistent with involves_human_subjects: false and direct_collection.is_direct: false; no consistency violation arises from the absence of consent documentation here.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition fails on the same external evidence from E1 (cell-line description and keywords) and E8 (instrument-based collection mechanisms, no recruitment). strengths: Identifier and platform integration are fully coherent: DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, publisher ROR:0153tk833, the dataverse.lib.virginia.edu landing page and the citation's V2 designation all agree, and the three predecessor releases are each separately citable by DOI with typed is_new_version_of relationships.

Funding transparency is complete and format-correct: three NIH awards (1OT2OD032742-01, 3OT2OD032742-01S2, 5U54HG012513-02) all parse against NIH conventions, with RePORTER application number, award amount, project period and recipient institution, plus correct representation of non-grant institutional support with no spurious grant block.

Limitations, biases and impacts form a consistent chain rather than three disconnected lists: is_representative false leads to selection_bias and sampling_bias with affected_subsets, which lead to a future_use_impacts entry about model generalizability, which is reinforced by the clinical-use prohibition.

Provenance is traceable in both directions — upstream to named per-modality depositions at MassIVE, NCBI SRA and Figshare with embargo status attached to the specific affected resources, and downstream through RO-Crate provenance graphs shipped in the release metadata archive, with raw_data/processed_data roles marked on every one of the ten archives.

The record is exceptionally disciplined about evidential scope: source_caveats at both dataset and field level declare where sources disagree and decline to assert release-level figures that are only known project-wide, rather than filling slots with plausible but unsupported values.
weaknesses: No software is named that produced or transformed the data actually distributed: every named tool belongs to the cell-map pipeline whose outputs the record says are not in this release, to RO-Crate packaging, to capture instrumentation, or to hosting, leaving the derivation of the released AP-MS, SEC-MS and Perturb-seq packages unattributed.

Variable-level metadata is entirely absent, and content formats inside the ZIP archives are undeclared, so a reuser cannot determine the internal structure, column semantics or file types of the processed packages before downloading them.

No errata and no change description for this release: updates.update_details carries only forward-looking cadence, and the only change narrative in the record concerns an earlier release, so what June 2026 changed relative to October 2025 is unknown.

The description claims MDA-MB-468 Perturb-seq data as part of this release while no such archive is listed and the corresponding deposition is recorded as embargoed — a contradiction that could send a user looking for data that is not there.

Version and cadence signals are confusing: this June 2026 release is version 2.0 while two earlier releases are recorded as 2.1, and the stated quarterly update frequency does not match the eight-month gap between the October 2025 and June 2026 releases.
recommendations: Attach used_software (with versions) to the processing strategies that produced the distributed packages — the mass-spectrometry search and quantification software behind the AP-MS and SEC-MS results, and the single-cell processing software behind the Perturb-seq atlas — keeping them distinct from the downstream cell-map tooling.

Add variables entries with identifiers, descriptions and units for the columns of the processed AP-MS, SEC-MS and Perturb-seq atlas tables, and declare per-collection content formats, media types and character encoding in addition to the ZIP container.

Record errata and a release note in updates.update_details stating what the June 2026 release adds, removes or corrects relative to the October 2025 release, and reconcile the version string with the series (or state explicitly that each quarterly deposit versions independently).
Correct the description so that release contents match file_collections: state that MDA-MB-468 Perturb-seq is embargoed and not distributed here, or add the corresponding archive.

Document preprocessing for the released data specifically, and either supply imputation_protocols or state explicitly that no imputation was performed; add release-level instance counts for the imaging archives so the scale of this release is determinable.
